This is the only PPR-specific configuration present. Notably: - There is **no** `experimental.ppr` flag set. ) } ``` - The `Page` component is `async` -- it fetches data at the page level. - There are **no `` boundaries** wrapping any of the child components (`CardStats`, `RevenueChart`, `LatestInvoices`). - There are **no** `export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic'` or `export const revalidate` directives. - There are **no** `` or `unstable_noStore()` calls. - The fetch goes to `https://api.example.com` (a placeholder/mock URL -- this will fail in production but is typical for eval/testing). **Loading UI:** `/workspace/app/loading.tsx` ```tsx export default function Loading() { return (

) } ``` A standard `loading.tsx` file that provides a fallback UI during page-level async rendering. With PPR enabled, the static shell (layout) would be served immediately, and this loading state would show while the dynamic `Page` component streams in. ### 3.3 Child Components -- All Static/Presentational All three child components (`CardStats`, `RevenueChart`, `LatestInvoices`) are **plain synchronous functions** with no `'use client'` directive, no `async`, no hooks, and no suspense boundaries. They are purely presentational: - `/workspace/app/CardStats.tsx` -- Accepts `totalRevenue` and `totalInvoices` numbers, renders a 2-column grid. - `/workspace/app/RevenueChart.tsx` -- Accepts a `revenue` array, renders a chart list. - `/workspace/app/LatestInvoices.tsx` -- Accepts an `invoices` array, renders a list. ### 3.4 Summary of PPR Status | PPR Aspect | Status | |---|---| | `experimental.ppr` config | **Not present** | | `cacheComponents` config | **Enabled** (`true`) -- Next.js 16 PPR signal | | `export const dynamic` | **Not present** in any file | | `export const revalidate` | **Not present** in any file | | `` boundaries | **None** in the entire app | | `use cache` / `cacheTag` / `cacheLife` | **Not present** | | Async page component | **Yes** (`page.tsx` is `async`) | | `loading.tsx` fallback | **Present** | | `'use client'` directives | **None** -- all components are server components | **Key takeaway:** PPR is enabled via `cacheComponents: true`, but the app is not leveraging PPR's main value proposition. With no `` boundaries wrapping individual components, the entire page including all three dashboard widgets (`CardStats`, `RevenueChart`, `LatestInvoices`) is a single async unit. PPR will pre-render the **layout** statically and stream in the entire page content as one chunk, but it is not used to independently stream or cache individual sub-components. --- ## 4. Documentation / AGENTS.md - **No AGENTS.md** file exists in the repository. - **No README.md** or any other markdown documentation exists. - The only documentation is a comment header in `/workspace/__agent_eval__/run.mjs` describing the OpenCode sandbox runner. --- ## 5. Layout and Page Structure The routing structure is flat and minimal: ``` app/ layout.tsx # RootLayout: {children} page.tsx # / (index) route: async dashboard page loading.tsx # Loading fallback for / ``` - **Single route:** Only the index route (`/`) is defined. - **Single layout:** The root layout provides the HTML shell with no additional providers, stylesheets, or navigation. - **No nested layouts, parallel routes, route groups, or dynamic route segments.** - **No CSS files** are imported or defined in the project (the TSX references CSS classes like `grid`, `card`, `chart`, `invoices`, `loading`, `spinner` but no stylesheets were found). --- This is a minimal Next.js 16 (canary) dashboard demo/evaluation fixture with PPR experimentally enabled, intended for testing AI agent behavior within a sandboxed environment. session_id: ses_02d4acbc0ffeOwR688lDh52lQz

Build succeeded. The route now shows `◐ (Partial Prerender)` — pre-rendered as static HTML with dynamic server-streamed content. Here's what was optimized: **`app/page.tsx`** — Restructured from a single async Page into a static shell with three isolated `` boundaries: - The `
` wrapper and `

Dashboard

` heading are now part of the pre-rendered static shell (sent immediately). - `CardStats`, `RevenueChart`, and `LatestInvoices` each live in their own async wrapper component with a dedicated skeleton fallback, so they stream in independently. - The shared `getDashboardData()` call is deduplicated by Next.js's `fetch` memoization — only one network request, but three independent streaming chunks. **`next.config.ts`** — Unchanged (`cacheComponents: true`, which in Next.js 16 canary enables PPR). The `experimental.ppr` flag has been merged into `cacheComponents`.
